body_md:
For $n \geq 3$, the Frobenius norm of $g^{-1}$ need not equal that of $g$. Consequently, the kernel \eqref{auto kernel count} (defined in terms of \eqref{automorphickernel}) lacks symmetry in $z,w$.
The orientation in \eqref{automorphickernel} determines the conjugations in the pre-trace formula. Keeping
that orientation avoids importing a rank-one symmetry which higher-rank norm balls do not possess.

title: Remark
body_md: The argument of our proof works for almost all pairs of points $(z,w)$, hence it cannot guarantee the bound for any \textit{specific} preassigned pair of points. The set $B_w$ in Theorem \ref{ourmainthm} does in general depend on $w$, and as such, does not produce any explicit point $z \in B_w$, a single full-measure set valid for all $w$ or any information for the diagonal case $z=w$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Our main Theorem \ref{ourmainthm} is similar in spirit with \cite{Jana1, Jana2}, where optimal almost-everywhere approximation results for dense rational orbits are studied (see also \cite{GGN}).

name: A coarse shell bound

title: Proof
body_md: The imaginary parameters lie in the $r$-dimensional trace-zero hyperplane. Its intersection with a box of side $O(L)$ is covered by $O_n(L^r)$ boxes of fixed side length. Choose an imaginary parameter ${\tau}$ as center in each of these boxes. The real parts remain in the fixed compact set $C_\rho$, so enlarging the radius by a fixed amount covers the corresponding complex parameters by the balls in Proposition \ref{local spectral density}. On each of these balls $\mathcal{W}(\tau)\ll_n L^m$. Summing the local estimate over all $O_n(L^r)$ balls gives the desired bound.

title: Remark
body_md: The contour argument distinguishes two different uniformity issues. The discs control coincidences of the complex poles ${\mu}_j-2k $ and the endpoint products \eqref{i_0 imaginary} control coincidences of the imaginary coordinates. Both are required for a statement uniform across the full automorphic spectrum. At an exact multiple pole, direct residue formulas contain powers of $\log T$. The small contour argument handles these and nearby poles at once; the resulting loss is the arbitrarily small factor $T^{\eta}$.

body_md:
Our original counting function has jumps and is not continuous. 
The assertion of continuity used above concerns only the smoothed kernels. Its values at the jump radii is controlled by the pointwise double inequality \eqref{sandwich}, which was proved with closed balls. Thus no exceptional set of radii is introduced when we apply the unsmoothing step.
